claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Becher et al., 2021; Wibmer et al., 2021; Herz et al., 2021.

claims.claim: BAT abundance and activity is associated with higher energy expenditure.
claims.source: Although the direct mechanisms have not been fully elucidated, BAT abundance and activity is associated with higher energy expenditure, altered secretion of hormones (Chondronikola et al., 2016; Géloën et al., 1988; Hanssen et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2015; Villarroya et al., 2017; Villarroya et al., 2019), and reduced visceral fat mass (Herz et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claims.claim: BAT abundance and activity is associated with altered secretion of hormones.
claims.source: Although the direct mechanisms have not been fully elucidated, BAT abundance and activity is associated with higher energy expenditure, altered secretion of hormones (Chondronikola et al., 2016; Géloën et al., 1988; Hanssen et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2015; Villarroya et al., 2017; Villarroya et al., 2019), and reduced visceral fat mass (Herz et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Chondronikola et al., 2016; Géloën et al., 1988; Hanssen et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2015; Villarroya et al., 2017; Villarroya et al., 2019.

claims.claim: BAT abundance and activity is associated with reduced visceral fat mass.
claims.source: Although the direct mechanisms have not been fully elucidated, BAT abundance and activity is associated with higher energy expenditure, altered secretion of hormones (Chondronikola et al., 2016; Géloën et al., 1988; Hanssen et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2015; Villarroya et al., 2017; Villarroya et al., 2019), and reduced visceral fat mass (Herz et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to Herz et al., 2021.

claims.claim: Cold exposure triggers BAT neogenesis in rodents.
claims.source: Cold exposure triggers BAT neogenesis and is an important adaptive means to increase the capacity for non-shivering thermogenesis in rodents (Bukowiecki et al., 1982; Bukowiecki et al., 1986; Foster and Frydman, 1978; Nedergaard, 1982; Nedergaard et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Bukowiecki et al., 1982; Bukowiecki et al., 1986; Foster and Frydman, 1978; Nedergaard, 1982; Nedergaard et al., 2019.

claims.claim: Fate mapping studies in rats indicated that brown adipocytes arise from interstitial cells that proliferate and differentiate during the first few days of cold exposure.
claims.source: Fate mapping studies in rats by Bukowiecki et al. strongly indicated that brown adipocytes (BAs) arise from interstitial cells that proliferate and differentiate during the first few days of cold exposure (Bukowiecki et al., 1986; Géloën et al., 1988).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Bukowiecki et al., 1986; Géloën et al., 1988.

claims.claim: Most, if not all, BAs induced by cold arise from stromal cells that express PDGFRA.
claims.source: More recently, genetic lineage-tracing experiments from our lab demonstrated that most, if not all, BAs induced by cold arise from stromal cells that express the surface marker platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha (PDGFRA).
claims.evidence: This is based on genetic lineage-tracing experiments from the authors' lab.

claims.claim: Cold exposure remodels the vasculature in BAT.
claims.source: In addition to effects on brown adipogenesis, cold exposure also remodels the vasculature, recruits monocytes/macrophages, and triggers proliferation of uncharacterized population(s) of cells that are potentially important for proper BAT expansion and remodeling (Lee et al., 2015; Géloën et al., 1988).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2015; Géloën et al., 1988.

claims.claim: Cold exposure recruits monocytes/macrophages to BAT.
claims.source: In addition to effects on brown adipogenesis, cold exposure also remodels the vasculature, recruits monocytes/macrophages, and triggers proliferation of uncharacterized population(s) of cells that are potentially important for proper BAT expansion and remodeling (Lee et al., 2015; Géloën et al., 1988).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2015; Géloën et al., 1988.

claims.claim: Recent single-cell transcriptional analysis indicates the existence of multiple stromal cell types in white adipose tissue depots that express PDGFRA.
claims.source: In this regard, recent single-cell transcriptional analysis indicates the existence of multiple stromal cell types in white adipose tissue (WAT) depots that express PDGFRA (Burl et al., 2018; Hepler et al., 2018; Merrick et al., 2019; Schwalie et al., 2018; Emont et al., 2022; Rondini and Granneman, 2020; Sárvári et al., 2021; Rondini et al., 2021), and that recruitment of brown/beige adipocytes in response to β3-adrenergic activation involves specific subsets of stromal cells and immune cells.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Burl et al., 2018; Hepler et al., 2018; Merrick et al., 2019; Schwalie et al., 2018; Emont et al., 2022; Rondini and Granneman, 2020; Sárvári et al., 2021; Rondini et al., 2021.

claims.claim: Recruitment of brown/beige adipocytes in response to β3-adrenergic activation involves specific subsets of stromal cells and immune cells.
claims.source: In this regard, recent single-cell transcriptional analysis indicates the existence of multiple stromal cell types in white adipose tissue (WAT) depots that express PDGFRA (Burl et al., 2018; Hepler et al., 2018; Merrick et al., 2019; Schwalie et al., 2018; Emont et al., 2022; Rondini and Granneman, 2020; Sárvári et al., 2021; Rondini et al., 2021), and that recruitment of brown/beige adipocytes in response to β3-adrenergic activation involves specific subsets of stromal cells and immune cells.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the cited single-cell transcriptional analysis studies.

claims.claim: Cold triggers proliferation of cells expressing the myeloid cell surface marker F4/80.
claims.source: In addition, we previously observed that cold triggers proliferation of cells expressing the myeloid cell surface marker F4/80, as well as uncharacterized population(s) of stromal cells (Lee et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2015.

claims.claim: Cold-induced mitogenesis in rodent BAT only commences after more than 2 days of cold exposure.
claims.source: Curiously, cold-induced mitogenesis in rodent BAT only commences after more than 2 days of cold exposure (Bukowiecki et al., 1982; Bukowiecki et al., 1986; Hunt and Hunt, 1967; Lee et al., 2015) and is concentrated within specific regions of the tissue (Lee et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Bukowiecki et al., 1982; Bukowiecki et al., 1986; Hunt and Hunt, 1967; Lee et al., 2015.

claims.claim: Cold-induced mitogenesis is concentrated within specific regions of the tissue.
claims.source: Curiously, cold-induced mitogenesis in rodent BAT only commences after more than 2 days of cold exposure (Bukowiecki et al., 1982; Bukowiecki et al., 1986; Hunt and Hunt, 1967; Lee et al., 2015) and is concentrated within specific regions of the tissue (Lee et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2015.

claims.claim: Cold-induced neogenesis in BAT requires intact sympathetic activity.
claims.source: Cold-induced neogenesis in BAT requires intact sympathetic activity that can be mimicked by systemic norepinephrine (NE) infusion in warm-adapted mice (Lee et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2015.

claims.claim: Systemic norepinephrine infusion can mimic cold-induced neogenesis in warm-adapted mice.
claims.source: Cold-induced neogenesis in BAT requires intact sympathetic activity that can be mimicked by systemic norepinephrine (NE) infusion in warm-adapted mice (Lee et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2015.

claims.claim: The effects of NE infusion are prevented by global knockout of ADRB1.
claims.source: Moreover, the effects of NE infusion are prevented by global knockout (KO) of the β1-adrenergic receptor (ADRB1) (Lee et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2015.

claims.claim: ADRB1, but not ADRB3, are present on ASC.
claims.source: ADRB1, but not β3-adrenergic receptors (ADRB3), are present on ASC, and in vitro experiments suggested that activation of preadipocyte ADRB1 mediates cold-induced BA neogenesis (Bronnikov et al., 1999; Bronnikov et al., 1992).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Bronnikov et al., 1999; Bronnikov et al., 1992.

claims.claim: In vitro experiments suggested that activation of preadipocyte ADRB1 mediates cold-induced BA neogenesis.
claims.source: ADRB1, but not β3-adrenergic receptors (ADRB3), are present on ASC, and in vitro experiments suggested that activation of preadipocyte ADRB1 mediates cold-induced BA neogenesis (Bronnikov et al., 1999; Bronnikov et al., 1992).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Bronnikov et al., 1999; Bronnikov et al., 1992.

claims.claim: K-means clustering of the top differentially expressed genes identified three distinct patterns of upregulated gene expression during cold exposure.
claims.source: K-means clustering of the top differentially expressed genes (DEGs) identified three distinct patterns of upregulated gene expression (Figure 1A).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claims.claim: Acutely upregulated genes were induced within 6 hours of cold exposure, but then returned to control levels after chronic cold acclimation.
claims.source: Acutely upregulated genes were induced within 6 hours of cold exposure, but then returned to control levels after chronic cold acclimation.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the RNA-seq time course analysis.

claims.claim: Acutely upregulated genes include Ppargc1a, Ucp1, Nr4a1, and Dio2.
claims.source: Genes in this cluster are well-known targets of protein kinase A (PKA), including peroxisome proliferative activated receptor gamma coactivator 1 alpha (Ppargc1a), uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1), nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 1 (Nr4a1), and iodothyronine deiodinase 2 (Dio2) (Figure 1A).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claims.claim: Chronically upregulated genes were induced following 1–2 days of cold exposure and remained elevated for the duration of the time in cold.
claims.source: Chronically upregulated genes were induced following 1–2 days of cold exposure and remained elevated for the duration of the time in cold.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the RNA-seq time course analysis.

claims.claim: Chronically upregulated genes include Elovl3, Fasn, and Pdk4.
claims.source: This cluster included genes involved in lipid synthesis and oxidation, such as elongation of very long chain fatty acids-like 3 (Elovl3), fatty acid synthase (Fasn), and pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase isoenzyme 4 (Pdk4).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the RNA-seq analysis.

claims.claim: The third cluster of genes showed delayed and variable upregulation among individual mice.
claims.source: The third cluster was interesting, as the gene upregulation was delayed and variable among individual mice.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the RNA-seq time course analysis.

claims.claim: The third cluster of genes included proliferation markers (Birc5, Top2a) and genes indicating innate immune activation and macrophage recruitment (Lgals3, Gpnmb, Trem2).
claims.source: Genes in this cluster included proliferation markers (Birc5, Top2a), as well as various genes indicating innate immune activation and macrophage recruitment (Lgals3, Gpnmb, Trem2) (Figure 1A).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claims.claim: Proliferation markers and immune cell recruitment markers were highly correlated and this relationship was largely independent of time spent in the cold.
claims.source: Importantly, these variables were highly correlated and this relationship was largely independent of time spent in the cold (Figure 1B; p<0.001).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from correlation analysis of the RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: Cell proliferation and immune cell recruitment peak around the fourth day of cold exposure.
claims.source: These data confirm that cell proliferation and immune cell recruitment are connected and peak around the fourth day of cold exposure.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the RNA-seq time course data.

claims.claim: Lineage marker negative (Lin-) cell libraries contained adipose stromal cells (Pdgfra+ ASCs), vascular cells, and proliferating/newly differentiating adipocytes.
claims.source: Lineage marker negative (Lin-) cell libraries contained adipose stromal cells (Pdgfra+ ASCs), vascular cells, and proliferating/newly differentiating adipocytes (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Clustering of scRNA-seq data from control and cold-exposed mice identified eight major clusters.
claims.source: Clustering of scRNA-seq data from control and cold-exposed mice identified eight major clusters, ranging from ~500 to 6,500 cells per cluster (Figure 2A, Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Three clusters were defined as ASCs based on their expression of Pdgfra, Cd34, and Ly6a.
claims.source: Three of these clusters were defined as ASCs based on their expression of common mesenchymal stem cell markers Pdgfra, Cd34, and lymphocyte antigen 6 complex locus A (Ly6a, a.k.a. Sca1) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A) that are often used for identification of adipocyte progenitors (Burl et al., 2018; Hepler et al., 2018; Merrick et al., 2019; Schwalie et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis with support from cited literature.

claims.claim: Two cell clusters were unique to cold-exposed mice.
claims.source: Separating data by treatment revealed that two cell clusters were unique to cold-exposed mice (circled; Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: One cold-unique cluster retained numerous ASC markers like Pdgfra.
claims.source: One cluster retained numerous ASC markers like Pdgfra, whereas the other was largely Pdgfra negative and expressed high levels of markers of proliferation (e.g. Birc5) and adipocyte differentiation (e.g. Car3) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: One cold-unique cluster was largely Pdgfra negative and expressed high levels of markers of proliferation and adipocyte differentiation.
claims.source: One cluster retained numerous ASC markers like Pdgfra, whereas the other was largely Pdgfra negative and expressed high levels of markers of proliferation (e.g. Birc5) and adipocyte differentiation (e.g. Car3) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: High-resolution clustering resolved three distinct ASC cell types prominent in iBAT controls: ASC1-3.
claims.source: This clustering resolved three distinct ASC cell types prominent in iBAT controls: ASC1-3 (Figure 2C, left).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the high-resolution scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: ASC1 selectively expressed Col5a3, Cxcl14, and Bmper.
claims.source: Thus, ASC1 selectively expressed collagen type V alpha 3 chain (Col5a3), C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 14 (Cxcl14), and the bone morphogenic protein (BMP)-binding endothelial regulator (Bmper) (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: ASC2 cells expressed Pi16, Dpp4, and Fbn1.
claims.source: Cells in ASC2 expressed secreted protease inhibitor peptidase inhibitor 16 (Pi16), surface glycoprotein dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (Dpp4), and the ECM component fibronectin (Fbn1).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claims.claim: ASC3 cells selectively expressed Gdf10, Clec11a, and Fbln1.
claims.source: ASC3 cells selectively expressed secreted ligand growth differentiation factor 10 (Gdf10), C-type lectin domain containing 11a (Clec11a), and fibulin1 (Fbln1) (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: High-resolution clustering identified three additional cell clusters in cold-exposed mice.
claims.source: High-resolution clustering identified three additional cell clusters in cold-exposed mice (Figure 2C, right).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the high-resolution scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: All three additional cold-induced clusters expressed ASC1-specific markers.
claims.source: All of these clusters expressed ASC1-specific markers; however, two of the clusters were primarily defined by genes for proliferation (Top2a, Birc5, Stmn1), and/or adipogenic differentiation (Pparg, Lpl, Nnat) (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: Cold exposure greatly reduced expression of genes involved in cholesterol biosynthesis, cell adhesion, and extracellular matrix organization in ASC1.
claims.source: Examination of the two ASC1 expression states indicated that cold activation greatly reduced expression of genes involved in cholesterol biosynthesis (sterol biosynthetic process; GO:0016126, p=2.8E-10), cell adhesion (GO:0007155, p=4.9E-2) and extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198, p=7.7E-7), and strongly induced expression of genes involved in immune system process (GO:0002376, p=2.2E-6), chemokine activity (GO:0008009, p=5.0E-3) and cell migration (GO:0016477, p=3.6E-4).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from Gene Ontology analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claims.claim: Cold exposure strongly induced expression of genes involved in immune system process, chemokine activity, and cell migration in ASC1.
claims.source: Examination of the two ASC1 expression states indicated that cold activation greatly reduced expression of genes involved in cholesterol biosynthesis (sterol biosynthetic process; GO:0016126, p=2.8E-10), cell adhesion (GO:0007155, p=4.9E-2) and extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198, p=7.7E-7), and strongly induced expression of genes involved in immune system process (GO:0002376, p=2.2E-6), chemokine activity (GO:0008009, p=5.0E-3) and cell migration (GO:0016477, p=3.6E-4).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from Gene Ontology analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claims.claim: ASC1 cells expressed higher levels of Pparg and its target genes, such as Lpl.
claims.source: In addition, ASC1 cells appeared highly poised for adipogenesis, expressing higher levels of the master adipocyte transcriptional regulator peroxisome proliferator activated receptor gamma (Pparg) and its target genes, such as lipoprotein lipase (Lpl) (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: Cells in the differentiating cluster selectively expressed Nnat that was transiently upregulated during differentiation and silenced in mature BAs.
claims.source: Notably, cells in the differentiating cluster selectively expressed the imprinted gene neuronatin (Nnat) that was transiently upregulated during differentiation and silenced in mature BAs (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: Numerous ASC1-specific marker genes were co-expressed in the proliferating and differentiating clusters.
claims.source: Numerous ASC1-specific marker genes were co-expressed in the proliferating and differentiating clusters (Figure 2D), indicating that expression of these genes persists as cell differentiated into BAs.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: None of the ASC2 and ASC3 markers were expressed in the proliferating/differentiating clusters.
claims.source: In contrast, none of the aforementioned ASC2 and ASC3 markers were expressed in these proliferating/differentiating clusters (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: Cold-activated ASC1 are the immediate progenitors of new BAs induced by cold exposure.
claims.source: From these data, we concluded that cold-activated ASC1 are the immediate progenitors of new BAs induced by cold exposure.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the scRNA-seq data.

claims.claim: Differentiating cells exhibited a clear trajectory along t-SNE2 that included loss of Pdgfra expression, transient proliferation (Birc5), and sequential upregulation of early (Cebpa) and late (Adipoq, Ucp1) markers of brown adipogenesis.
claims.source: In addition, differentiating cells exhibited a clear trajectory along t-SNE2 that included loss of ASC marker expression (Pdgfra), transient proliferation (Birc5), and sequential upregulation of early (Cebpa) and late (Adipoq, Ucp1) markers of brown adipogenesis (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: Proliferating, non-differentiating cells that retained ASC1 marker expression did not appear to contribute to adipogenesis and might function to replenish the ASC1 population.
claims.source: In contrast, the proliferating, non-differentiating cells that retained ASC1 marker expression did not appear to contribute to adipogenesis and might function to replenish the ASC1 population, as suggested by previous fate mapping studies (Lee et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation based on the scRNA-seq data and previous fate mapping studies.

claims.claim: Interstitial ASC1 cells are highly responsive to cold exposure and comprise most, if not all, BA progenitors during acute cold-induced neogenesis.
claims.source: In summary, analysis of BAT ASCs and total stromal cell populations indicates that interstitial ASC1 cells are highly responsive to cold exposure and comprise most, if not all, BA progenitors during acute cold-induced neogenesis.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the scRNA-seq and spatial analysis data.

claims.claim: ASC1 comprised the majority of the PDGFRA+ parenchymal interstitial cells.
claims.source: Using smFISH, we found that while ASC1 comprised the majority of the PDGFRA+ parenchymal interstitial cells, ASC2 were localized to the tissue fascia and surrounding large vessels, whereas ASC3 were predominately localized to areas surrounding vessels, but not capillaries (Figure 3B–C).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the smFISH analysis shown in Figure 3B–C.

claims.claim: ASC2 were localized to the tissue fascia and surrounding large vessels.
claims.source: Using smFISH, we found that while ASC1 comprised the majority of the PDGFRA+ parenchymal interstitial cells, ASC2 were localized to the tissue fascia and surrounding large vessels, whereas ASC3 were predominately localized to areas surrounding vessels, but not capillaries (Figure 3B–C).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the smFISH analysis shown in Figure 3B–C.

claims.claim: ASC3 were predominately localized to areas surrounding vessels, but not capillaries.
claims.source: Using smFISH, we found that while ASC1 comprised the majority of the PDGFRA+ parenchymal interstitial cells, ASC2 were localized to the tissue fascia and surrounding large vessels, whereas ASC3 were predominately localized to areas surrounding vessels, but not capillaries (Figure 3B–C).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the smFISH analysis shown in Figure 3B–C.

claims.claim: The interstitial location of ASC1 is consistent with the work of Bukowiecki et al., 1986 who concluded that cold-induced brown adipocytes are derived from interstitial stromal cells.
claims.source: Importantly, the interstitial location of ASC1 is consistent with the work of Bukowiecki et al., 1986 who, using electron microscopy, concluded that cold-induced brown adipocytes are derived from interstitial stromal cells.
claims.evidence: This is a comparison of the current findings with previous work cited.

claims.claim: Nnat expression marks the transient state of early differentiation.
claims.source: Among genes expressed within the adipogenic trajectory, we found that Nnat was induced during early differentiation, then silenced upon terminal differentiation (Figure 4A). Thus, Nnat expression marks the transient state of early differentiation.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: Cold exposure triggered the appearance of numerous Top2a+ Dcn+ cells and clusters of Nnat positive cells.
claims.source: In contrast, cold exposure triggered the appearance of numerous Top2a+ Dcn+ cells, as well as clusters of Nnat positive cells with and without co-expression of Top2a (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the smFISH analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: High-resolution three-dimensional confocal imaging provided strong evidence for an adipogenic trajectory within a tissue niche.
claims.source: High-resolution three-dimensional confocal imaging provided strong evidence for an adipogenic trajectory within a tissue niche.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the confocal imaging data.

claims.claim: Proliferating ASC1 were observed immediately adjacent to proliferating/differentiating ASC1, and more distally to differentiating ASC1 lacking expression of proliferation markers.
claims.source: Thus, we observed proliferating ASC1 immediately adjacent to proliferating/differentiating ASC1, and more distally to differentiating ASC1 lacking expression of proliferation markers.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the high-resolution confocal imaging.

claims.claim: The majority of Nnat+ cells co-expressed the ASC1 marker Bmper, but not the ASC2 marker Pi16.
claims.source: As anticipated from scRNA-seq data, the majority of Nnat+ cells co-expressed the ASC1 marker Bmper, but not the ASC2 marker Pi16 (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the smFISH analysis shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Tamoxifen treatment reduced Adrb1 expression in ASC1 by more than 90%.
claims.source: Tamoxifen treatment reduced Adrb1 expression in ASC1 by more than 90% (chi-square p<0.00001, Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis of Adrb1 KO mice shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: Knockdown of Adrb1 in ASC1 had no discernable effect on the ability of cold exposure to increase ASC1 proliferation/differentiation.
claims.source: Surprisingly, we found that knockdown of Adrb1 in ASC1 had no discernable effect on the ability of cold exposure to increase ASC1 proliferation/differentiation (both being ~10 fold over basal in WT and Adrb1 KO mice) (Table 1, Supplementary file 4, and Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the Adrb1 KO experiments shown in Table 1 and Figure 5C.

claims.claim: Adrb1 knockout in ASCs had no significant effect on cold-induced expression of proliferation markers at the whole tissue level.
claims.source: In a larger independent cohort of mice, we found that Adrb1 knockout in ASCs had no significant effect on cold-induced expression of proliferation makers at the whole tissue level (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the qPCR analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: Cold induced the appearance of differentiating Nnat+ preadipocytes in the absence of detectible Adrb1 mRNA following Pdgfra-CreERT2-mediated recombination.
claims.source: In addition, smFISH demonstrated that cold induced the appearance of differentiating Nnat+ preadipocytes in the absence of detectible Adrb1 mRNA following Pdgfra-CreERT2-mediated recombination (p<0.00001; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, C).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the smFISH analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, C.

claims.claim: ASC Adrb1 expression is not required for cold-induced BA neogenesis.
claims.source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that ASC Adrb1 expression is not required for cold-induced BA neogenesis.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Adrb1 KO experiments.

claims.claim: 68–72% of the total individual variation in proliferation marker expression across treatment groups was accounted for by variation in markers of immune cell recruitment.
claims.source: However, while Adrb1 expression did not impact neogenesis, 68–72% of the total individual variation in proliferation marker expression (Birc5, Top2a) across treatment groups was accounted for by variation in markers of immune cell recruitment (Trem2, Gpnmb; Figure 5E).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from correlation analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claims.claim: BAs express ADRB1 and, owing to its higher affinity for NE, is a major receptor for mediating cold-induced metabolic activation.
claims.source: BAs also express ADRB1 and, owing to its higher affinity for NE, is a major receptor for mediating cold-induced metabolic activation (Bukowiecki et al., 1978; Chaudhry and Granneman, 1999).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Bukowiecki et al., 1978; Chaudhry and Granneman, 1999.

claims.claim: CL treatment triggered significant activation, proliferation and differentiation of ASC1 cells.
claims.source: We found that CL treatment triggered significant activation, proliferation and differentiation of ASC1 cells (Table 1, Supplementary file 5, Supplementary file 6, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-F).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the CL treatment experiments shown in Table 1 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-F.

claims.claim: Cold exposure triggers progenitor proliferation/differentiation indirectly via adrenergic activation of BAs and not through direct ADRB1 activation of progenitors.
claims.source: Taken together, these data strongly suggest that cold exposure triggers progenitor proliferation/differentiation indirectly via adrenergic activation of BAs and not through direct ADRB1 activation of progenitors.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Adrb1 KO and CL treatment experiments.

claims.claim: scRNA-seq identified 16 immune clusters in lineage positive (Lin+) cells from mice at RT or exposed to cold.
claims.source: To gain insight into the immune cell complexity of mouse iBAT, we used scRNA-seq to profile lineage positive (Lin+) cells from mice at RT or exposed to cold and identified 16 immune clusters (Figure 6A and Supplementary file 7).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: Seven immune clusters were different subpopulations of macrophages and dendritic cells, comprising 52.0% of the cells in the Lin+ dataset.
claims.source: Seven of these clusters were different subpopulations of macrophages and dendritic cells (MAC and DEND, respectively), comprising 52.0% of the cells in this dataset.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claims.claim: Cold exposure dramatically altered the immune cell landscape in mouse iBAT and led to the expansion of dendritic cells and altered phenotype/subtypes of macrophages.
claims.source: Cold exposure dramatically altered the immune cell landscape in mouse iBAT and led to the expansion of dendritic cells and altered phenotype/subtypes of macrophages (Figure 6B, circled).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: All four dendritic cell clusters increased with cold exposure.
claims.source: All four dendritic cell clusters increased with cold exposure (DEND1-4; Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: DEND1 cells expressed conventional dendritic cell type 1 (cDC1) markers, including high levels of Irf8, Ppt1, Jaml, and Naaa.
claims.source: DEND1 cells expressed conventional dendritic cell type 1 (cDC1) markers, including high levels of the master transcriptional regulator Irf8, as well as genes Ppt1, Jaml, and Naaa (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A; Guilliams and van de Laar, 2015; Hilligan and Ronchese, 2020).

results.result: RNA-seq time course analysis identified three distinct patterns of gene upregulation during cold exposure: acute (within 6 hours, returning to baseline), chronic (1-2 days, sustained), and delayed/variable (including proliferation and immune markers). Proliferation and immune cell recruitment markers were highly correlated (p<0.001) independent of time in cold, peaking around day 4.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C43 provide converging evidence from RNA-seq analysis showing temporal gene expression patterns and strong correlation between proliferation and immune markers. The k-means clustering approach is appropriate, and the correlation analysis (Figure 1B) demonstrates statistical significance with r²=0.731 and r²=0.788 for different marker pairs.

results.result: scRNA-seq identified three ASC subpopulations (ASC1, ASC2, ASC3) distinguished by differential expression of ECM and signaling genes. Cold exposure induced two additional clusters expressing ASC1 markers plus proliferation/differentiation markers, indicating ASC1 activation and adipogenic commitment.
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C55 describe comprehensive scRNA-seq characterization with appropriate clustering methods and marker gene identification. The identification of ASC subtypes is well-supported by differential gene expression analysis and validated by multiple marker genes per subtype.

results.result: Cold-activated ASC1 showed reduced expression of cholesterol biosynthesis and ECM genes while inducing immune/chemokine genes. ASC1 cells expressed high Pparg levels and showed an adipogenic trajectory with transient Nnat expression during differentiation, with only ASC1 markers (not ASC2/ASC3) present in proliferating/differentiating clusters.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C65 are supported by Gene Ontology analysis with significant p-values (p<10E-6) and clear trajectory analysis showing sequential marker expression. The conclusion that ASC1 are progenitors (C62, C65) is well-supported by the marker co-expression patterns.

results.result: smFISH spatial analysis revealed distinct tissue localization: ASC1 in parenchymal interstitium, ASC2 in fascia/large vessels, and ASC3 around vessels but not capillaries. This spatial distribution is consistent with historical electron microscopy findings.
results.evaluation: Claims C66-C69 provide spatial validation of scRNA-seq findings using orthogonal smFISH methodology. The consistency with Bukowiecki et al. 1986 (C69) strengthens the interpretation, though this relies on accurate citation of prior work.

results.result: High-resolution imaging revealed an adipogenic trajectory in tissue niches, with Nnat marking transient early differentiation. Cold exposure induced clusters of proliferating (Top2a+Dcn+) and differentiating (Nnat+) cells, with Nnat+ cells co-expressing ASC1 marker Bmper but not ASC2 marker Pi16.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C74 demonstrate spatial adipogenic trajectory using complementary imaging approaches. The quantification in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B provides statistical support, though sample size (n=3 animals) is modest.

results.result: Tamoxifen-induced Adrb1 knockout in ASC1 (>90% reduction) did not prevent cold-induced ASC1 proliferation/differentiation (~10-fold increase in both WT and KO). This was confirmed by scRNA-seq, qPCR, and smFISH showing Nnat+ preadipocytes appearing despite Adrb1 absence.
results.evaluation: Claims C75-C79 present a surprising negative result with multiple lines of evidence (scRNA-seq, qPCR, smFISH). The >90% knockdown efficiency (C75) is well-documented, and the lack of effect on proliferation/differentiation is demonstrated across multiple assays. Statistical analysis (chi-square p<0.00001) supports the conclusion.

results.result: Despite Adrb1 not being required in ASCs, 68-72% of variation in proliferation markers correlated with immune cell recruitment markers. ADRB3 agonist (CL316,243) treatment, which activates brown adipocytes expressing ADRB3, was sufficient to induce ASC1 proliferation and differentiation, suggesting indirect signaling from activated adipocytes.
results.evaluation: Claims C80-C83 provide strong correlative evidence (r²=0.68-0.72) and functional validation via pharmacological ADRB3 activation. The conclusion of indirect signaling (C83) is well-supported by the combination of negative (Adrb1 KO) and positive (CL treatment) results, though the specific mechanisms remain to be elucidated.

results.result: scRNA-seq of Lin+ cells identified 16 immune clusters including 7 macrophage/dendritic cell subpopulations (52% of cells). Cold exposure dramatically altered immune landscape, expanding dendritic cells (DEND1-4) and recruiting lipid-handling MAC1 and interferon-activated MAC3 macrophages while reducing resident MAC2. Proliferation occurred mainly in cDC1 and moDC, not macrophages.
results.evaluation: Claims C84-C101 provide comprehensive immune cell characterization with appropriate marker-based identification supported by literature citations. The phenotypic assignments are consistent with known dendritic cell and macrophage markers, though some assignments rely on limited marker sets.

results.result: ASC1 proliferation/differentiation strongly correlated with recruitment of cDC1 (r²=0.74), moDC (r²=0.91), and MAC1 (r²=0.87) across diverse experimental conditions (cold, CL treatment, Adrb1 KO). This relationship remained significant even excluding basal values.
results.evaluation: Claims C102-C103 demonstrate robust correlations across multiple experimental manipulations, strengthening causal inference. The high r² values and persistence after excluding controls suggest a genuine biological relationship, though correlation does not prove causation.

results.result: Histological analysis revealed cold-induced recruitment of GPNMB+ MAC1 and MHCII+ dendritic cells to specific locations: within 50μm of tissue borders and near acellular vacancies (sites of adipocyte efferocytosis). Nearly all proliferating ASC1 (MKI67+PDGFRA+) were in close proximity to F4/80+ immune cells, with ASC1 processes extending toward and contacting immune cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C112 provide detailed spatial characterization using high-resolution confocal microscopy. The identification of efferocytosis sites (C111) is an inference based on morphological features (vacancies lacking PLIN1, ~20μm diameter, lipid remnants), which is reasonable but not definitively proven without additional markers.

results.result: smFISH and EdU pulse-chase experiments demonstrated dynamic spatial relationships: proliferating progenitors closely associated with H2-Ab1+ dendritic cells, with this association declining 4-5 fold upon differentiation. MHCII+ DCs were 3× more likely to be within 10μm of dividing versus differentiated adipocytes (27.3% vs 9.35%, p=0.00013). Non-differentiating progenitors maintained close contact with MHCII+ cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C113-C118 demonstrate temporal dynamics using EdU labeling and spatial analysis. The statistical analysis (p=0.00013, n=267 cells) supports the proximity differences, though the sample size across only 2-3 mice is modest. The conclusion of dynamic niche formation/resolution (C118) is well-supported by the spatial-temporal data.

results.result: Ligand-receptor analysis identified potential cell-cell communication mechanisms including Spp1 (from MAC1) binding to Cd44/Sdc1 (on ASC1), and cold-induced upregulation of Adam12 in ASC1. These molecules have established roles in progenitor recruitment and adipogenesis based on prior literature.
results.evaluation: Claims C119-C126 identify potential signaling mechanisms through computational ligand-receptor analysis and expression patterns. However, these remain hypothetical interactions without functional validation. The claims appropriately rely on prior literature for functional roles (C119, C121, C122, C124-C126), but direct testing of these interactions in the BAT neogenesis context is needed.

results.result: Independent lineage tracing using Pdgfra-CreERT2 x LSL-tdTomato confirmed 100% (258/258, n=5 mice) of new brown adipocytes derived from Pdgfra+ cells. Myf5 was not expressed in any adult stromal cell subtype, indicating Pdgfra+ ASC1 are the immediate progenitors of cold-induced brown adipocytes in adult iBAT.
results.evaluation: Claims C127-C129 provide definitive lineage tracing evidence with complete penetrance (100%, n=258 cells). The absence of Myf5 in adult stromal cells (C128) clarifies developmental versus adult progenitor populations. The conclusion (C129) is well-supported by converging scRNA-seq and genetic tracing data.

results.result: The authors conclude that cold-induced neogenesis is an indirect adaptive response to chronic brown adipocyte activation and elevated metabolic demand, rather than a reflexive response to β-adrenergic signaling in progenitors. This serves to match thermogenic capacity to thermogenic demand.
results.evaluation: Claims C130, C12, C13 represent the central mechanistic conclusion integrating multiple experimental findings: Adrb1 KO in ASCs had no effect, ADRB3 activation was sufficient, immune cell recruitment correlated with neogenesis, and the process was delayed (2-3 days). While the indirect mechanism is well-supported, the specific signals from stressed adipocytes remain to be identified.

results.result: Background claims establish that cold exposure triggers BAT neogenesis involving β-adrenergic signaling, PDGFRA+ ASC proliferation, and immune cell recruitment. BAT is metabolically active in adults and associated with healthier metabolic profiles. Prior work suggested ADRB1 on preadipocytes mediates neogenesis, though the delayed onset (>2 days) and regional specificity were unexplained.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C34 provide literature context supported by appropriate citations. These establish the knowledge gaps that motivated the current study. The citations appear relevant, though detailed verification of each cited claim is beyond this evaluation's scope.

results.result: The study identifies interstitial ASC1 as direct precursors of new brown adipocytes, comprising most if not all BA progenitors during cold-induced neogenesis.
results.evaluation: This result is already captured in the comprehensive ASC characterization result above. Claims C5, C62, C65 represent the same conclusion stated at different points in the manuscript.
